rooms.title: Precinct Front Desk
rooms.description: Dana starts her shift. Sergeant Prakash gives the pharmacy assignment, case file and camera; the bulletin board and dispatch repeat details. At the end, Dana files the case here (wrong-tray gag, paperwork corrections). Street door (south) is gated until the assignment is received.

rooms.title: Records Office
rooms.description: A records clerk and filing cabinets. Dana checks Quayside Freight's delivery ledger: the driver's truck logged a stop at a Pier Road warehouse the night of the break-in. Taking the ledger copy is key evidence.

rooms.title: Main Street
rooms.description: Quiet brick shopfronts and a blue-and-white patrol car. Officer Bud Bukowski waits with delivery driver Tommy Vance by his Quayside Freight van. Dana checks his story and finds a discrepancy (his route sheet says he never had a Hollis stop at 6 AM). Hub between the precinct, pharmacy and Pier Road.

rooms.title: Hollis Pharmacy
rooms.description: The break-in scene. Dana photographs the forced back door and collects a dropped pill bottle with a Quayside Freight crate label. The frightened pharmacist, once shown the badge, admits the delivery company pressured her and names the Pier Road warehouse.

rooms.title: Pier Road
rooms.description: Outside the Quayside Freight warehouse by the water. Bud warns Dana not to go in alone; she must radio dispatch for backup first. Entering without backup ends the case.

rooms.title: Quayside Warehouse
rooms.description: Stolen pharmacy stock in crates. With backup called and the evidence in hand (ledger, bottle, photos, driver discrepancy), Dana confronts and arrests the suspect, warehouse foreman Carl Denning. Then she returns to Prakash to file the report.

facts.name: protagonist
facts.text: Officer Dana Reyes, rookie, first week on the Millhaven PD. Navy uniform, cap, duty belt. Ego view 0 (loops right, left, down, up). Carries badge (item 0) and radio (item 1).

facts.name: inventory
facts.text: Items: 0 badge (carried), 1 radio (carried), 2 case file (given by Prakash in room 1), 3 camera (given by Prakash in room 1), 4 pill bottle (room 4), 5 ledger copy (room 2), 6 incident report (written after the arrest).

facts.name: case
facts.text: Hollis Pharmacy, 14 Main Street, broken into overnight. Reported at 6:10 AM by driver Tommy Vance of Quayside Freight, who claims he found the back door open on his route. Truth: his route sheet has no Hollis stop, and the ledger logs his truck at the Pier Road warehouse at 2 AM. Foreman Carl Denning ran the theft and stores the stock at the warehouse.

facts.name: scoring
facts.text: Max 215 (v7). 10 assignment (room 1, f30), 25 driver discrepancy (room 3, f32), 30 pharmacy documented + evidence (room 4, f33), 40 records/witness link to warehouse (room 2/4, f34), 60 backup + arrest (rooms 5-6, f35/f36), 50 case filed at Prakash's desk (room 1, f37). Each awarded once.

facts.name: flags
facts.text: f30 assigned, f31 intro seen, f32 driver discrepancy, f33 pharmacy documented, f34 warehouse linked, f35 backup called, f36 suspect arrested, f37 case filed. v40 picture temp, v41 radio blink speed, v42/v43 ego pos temp.

facts.name: dispatch
facts.text: Radio/call dispatch works anywhere; dispatch is patient and dry and repeats the current lead.

facts.name: prakash
facts.text: Sergeant Prakash has two trays on his desk: IN, and one for forms filed in the wrong tray. Room 1 must later handle 'file report' when f36 is set and item 6 is carried: incomplete paperwork (missing evidence) gets sent back for correction; complete filing sets f37 and awards 50.

facts.name: bud
facts.text: Officer Bud Bukowski, Dana's partner: talks too much, brave when it counts. Waits on Main Street, then at Pier Road warns Dana not to enter alone.

The base template: menus, death and fallbacks

New games are seeded with editable boilerplate before the first room. Use it as a recommended starting point when it fits, or extend or replace any part to serve the brief. These are ordinary game resources, with no protected ownership or reserved template ranges.

- Logic 0 builds the menu bar once on boot (File: Save, Restore, Restart, Quit; Speed; Sound; Help), binds the classic keys (ESC opens the menu, F5/F7/F9 save, restore and restart, F1 shows help, TAB lists the inventory), turns the status line on, then runs call.v(v0) so your room logic runs first every cycle. After the room returns, logic 0 answers the menu controllers and, once per submitted line, prints the parser fallback: "I don't know the word" when the line carried an unknown word, "I don't understand that" when no said() matched. A room that answers a line without a said() match should set(f4) after its own reply so the template does not add the generic one.
- Death is a shared handler: print your death line, then call(255). It stops input and movement, plays the death sound and offers the Restore, Restart or Quit box — SPACE steps the choice, ENTER confirms, 1-3 choose directly, F7/F9/Alt-Z answer directly. A cancelled or failed restore returns to the box; the player stays dead rather than walking in a broken control mode. If you replace this handler, design and playtest the recovery or continuation behavior your game needs.
- Read logic 0 and logic 255 for their current state, controller and string usage before editing; their sources are available through read_logic. Update affected references together when reusing IDs or changing conventions. Automatic allocation avoids IDs used by the current code; explicit bindings and edits can coordinate a rewrite. Playtest boot, input and any menu/death behavior affected by your changes. A fair death still needs a fair cause: the hazard belongs in your room's picture and priority plane.
